senses.definition_en: bring (something) into existence

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo a bōpa motho ka setšoantšo sa hae.
usage_example.english: So God created man in His own image.

senses.definition_en: to prepare and use land for crops

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho se lema le ho se hlokomela.
usage_example.english: ...to tend and keep it.

senses.definition_en: to feel embarrassed or guilty

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha baa ka ba hlajoa ke lihlong.
usage_example.english: ...were not ashamed.

senses.definition_en: a snake; a treacherous person

usage_example.sesotho: Joale noha e ne e le seli ka ho fetisisa.
usage_example.english: Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast.

senses.definition_en: to invoke evil upon; to damn

usage_example.sesotho: u rohakiloe har’a liphoofolo tsohle.
usage_example.english: You are cursed more than all cattle.

senses.definition_en: the outward appearance or apparent form of something

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo... o ile a mo etsa ka sebōpeho sa Molimo.
usage_example.english: God... made him in the likeness of God.

senses.definition_en: to bring a child into existence by the process of reproduction

usage_example.sesotho: Adama... a tsoala mora ea tšoanang le eena.
usage_example.english: Adam... begot a son in his own likeness.

senses.definition_en: the easing or alleviation of a person's feelings of grief or distress

usage_example.sesotho: Enoa o tla re tlisetsa matšeliso mosebetsing oa rōna.
usage_example.english: This one will comfort us concerning our work.

senses.definition_en: an overflowing of a large amount of water over what is normally dry land

usage_example.sesotho: ke tlisa moroallo oa metsi holim ’a lefatše.
usage_example.english: I am bringing floodwaters on the earth.

senses.definition_en: an ancient measure of length based on the forearm

usage_example.sesotho: ...bolelele ba areka e be litsoe tse makholo a mararo.
usage_example.english: ...the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits.

senses.definition_en: a natural spring or source of water

usage_example.sesotho: mehloli eohle ea boliba bo boholo ea phunyeha.
usage_example.english: all the fountains of the great deep were broken up.

senses.definition_en: to continue to exist after others have ceased to do so

usage_example.sesotho: ke Noe feela le ba nang le eena... ba ileng ba sala.
usage_example.english: Only Noah and those who were with him... remained alive.

senses.definition_en: to become less intense, violent, or severe; (of water) to sink to a lower level

usage_example.sesotho: metsi a qala ho kokobela.
usage_example.english: the waters subsided.

senses.definition_en: the process or period of gathering in crops

usage_example.sesotho: ha ho mohla ho jaloa ha peō le kotulo... li tla khaotsa.
usage_example.english: seedtime and harvest... shall not cease.

senses.definition_en: the domain or territory over which a king or government rules

usage_example.sesotho: ’Muso oa hae o ile oa simoloha Babele.
usage_example.english: His kingdom began at Babel.

senses.definition_en: the edge or boundary of a territory

usage_example.sesotho: moeli oa Mokanana oa e-ba ho tloha Sidone.
usage_example.english: the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon.

morphology.derivation: From verb 'jaka' (to reside away from home)

senses.definition_en: a person who resides temporarily in a place

usage_example.sesotho: Abrame a theohela nģ’a Egepeta ho ea lula teng e le mojaki.
usage_example.english: Abram went down to Egypt to dwell there as a sojourner.

senses.definition_en: the owner or keeper of a herd of domesticated animals

usage_example.sesotho: ...pakeng tsa balisa ba ka le balisa ba hao.
usage_example.english: ...between my herdsmen and your herdsmen.

senses.definition_en: close relatives or people treated as brothers

usage_example.sesotho: ...etsoe re bara ba motho.
usage_example.english: ...for we are brethren.

senses.definition_en: to be in a state of possessing many assets, especially livestock

usage_example.sesotho: Abrame o ne a ruile mehlape e mengata.
usage_example.english: Abram was very rich in livestock.

senses.definition_en: the right-hand side; often associated with strength or the South in Southern Sotho orientation

usage_example.sesotho: haeba u e-ea ka ho le letona...
usage_example.english: if you go to the right...

senses.definition_en: a precious shiny grayish-white metal

usage_example.sesotho: ...o ne a ruile... silevera le khauta.
usage_example.english: ...he was rich... in silver and gold.

senses.definition_en: supplied with water, especially land for crops or livestock

usage_example.sesotho: e ne e le sebaka se noselitsoeng hantle.
usage_example.english: it was a well-watered area.

senses.definition_en: the measurement or extent of something from side to side

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho ea ka bolelele ba eona le bophara ba eona.
usage_example.english: ...according to its length and its width.

senses.definition_en: people who commit immoral acts or transgressions against God

usage_example.sesotho: Banna ba Sodoma... e le baetsalibe ba baholo.
usage_example.english: The men of Sodom... were great sinners.

senses.definition_en: the condition of being imprisoned or confined

usage_example.sesotho: ...hore mor’abo o isitsoe kholehong.
usage_example.english: ...that his brother was taken captive.

senses.definition_en: to set free from imprisonment, danger, or difficulty

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba o lopolla thepa eohle.
usage_example.english: So he brought back (rescued) all the goods.

senses.definition_en: a male ruler of an independent state or tribe

usage_example.sesotho: ...marena ana a loantša Bera.
usage_example.english: ...these kings made war with Bera.

senses.definition_en: a formal agreement or alliance between parties

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba ne ba entse selekane le Abrame.
usage_example.english: ...they were allies (had a covenant) with Abram.

senses.definition_en: the state of being held as a prisoner or captive

usage_example.sesotho: ...mor’abo o isitsoe kholehong.
usage_example.english: ...his brother was taken captive.

senses.definition_en: to recover something or someone that was lost or taken

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba o lopolla thepa eohle.
usage_example.english: So he brought back (rescued) all the goods.

senses.definition_en: one-tenth of annual produce or earnings, given as a tax or offering

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Abrame o mo fa karolo ea leshome.
usage_example.english: And Abram gave him a tithe (tenth).

senses.definition_en: a person legally entitled to the property or rank of another on that person's death

usage_example.sesotho: ...mora oa ba ntlo ea ka o tla ntlhahlama e le mojalefa.
usage_example.english: ...a member of my household will succeed me as heir.

senses.definition_en: to cause someone to suffer or to treat them with persistent cruelty

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka sebele ba tla e hlorisa ka lilemo tse makholo a mane.
usage_example.english: ...they will surely afflict them for four hundred years.

senses.definition_en: to determine the total number of items

usage_example.sesotho: u bale linaleli, haeba u ka khona ho li bala.
usage_example.english: count the stars, if you are able to number them.

senses.definition_en: to cut through or divide into longitudinal pieces

usage_example.sesotho: ...eaba oa li khekhetha ’me o matahanya mokhekhetho.
usage_example.english: ...and he cut them in two and placed the pieces opposite each other.

senses.definition_en: to treat with cruelty or weight down with hardship

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka sebele ba tla e hlorisa.
usage_example.english: ...they will surely afflict them.

senses.definition_en: a structure for high-heat fire; used as a symbol of God's presence

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha feta sebōpi se kubellang mosi.
usage_example.english: ...there passed a smoking furnace.

senses.definition_en: A divine message or authoritative decree.

usage_example.sesotho: lentsoe la Jehova la tlela Abrame ponong.
usage_example.english: the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision.

senses.definition_en: Payment or prize for service or fidelity.

usage_example.sesotho: Moputso oa hao o tla ba moholo haholo.
usage_example.english: Your reward shall be very great.

senses.definition_en: One who exercises supreme control or government.

usage_example.sesotho: ’Musi Morena Jehova...
usage_example.english: Lord GOD (Sovereign Lord)...

senses.definition_en: One who legally succeeds to property or title.

usage_example.sesotho: ...o tla u hlahlama e le mojalefa.
usage_example.english: ...will succeed you as heir.

senses.definition_en: To divide longitudinally into two opposite halves.

usage_example.sesotho: eaba oa li khekhetha ’me o matahanya mokhekhetho.
usage_example.english: he cut them in two and placed each piece opposite the other.

senses.definition_en: A state of great fear or unsettling darkness.

usage_example.sesotho: ...lefifi le leholo ka mokhoa o tšosang.
usage_example.english: ...horror and great darkness.

senses.definition_en: Temporary residents in a land not their own.

usage_example.sesotho: ...peō ea hao e tla ba bajaki naheng eo.
usage_example.english: ...your descendants will be strangers in a land.

senses.definition_en: A burning stick or light source.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le serumula sa mollo.
usage_example.english: ...and a burning torch.

morphology.derivation: Diminutive form often used for household servants

senses.definition_en: A female domestic servant or slave.

usage_example.sesotho: ...o ne a e-na le lekhabunyane la Moegepeta.
usage_example.english: ...she had an Egyptian maidservant.

senses.definition_en: To become insignificant or hated in the eyes of another.

usage_example.sesotho: ...mong’a hae Sarai a qala ho nyeliseha mahlong a hae.
usage_example.english: ...her mistress Sarai was despised in her eyes.

senses.definition_en: To strip of honor; to treat with cruelty or indignity.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Sarai o qala ho le tlotlolla.
usage_example.english: Then Sarai dealt harshly with her.

senses.definition_en: To place oneself under the authority of another.

usage_example.sesotho: ...khutlela ho mong’a hao Sarai ’me u ikokobetse.
usage_example.english: ...return to your mistress and submit yourself.

senses.definition_en: The God who is vigilant and sees the individual in their distress.

usage_example.sesotho: U Molimo oa pono.
usage_example.english: You are the God-Who-Sees.

senses.definition_en: A wild ass or zebra; a metaphor for untamable freedom and nomadism.

usage_example.sesotho: ...o tla fetoha monna ea kang qoaha.
usage_example.english: ...he will become a man like a wild donkey.

senses.definition_en: Living without fault, guilt, or moral blemish.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u be ea se nang molato.
usage_example.english: ...and be blameless.

senses.definition_en: Without limit or end; eternal and unmeasured in duration.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bakeng sa selekane ho isa nakong e sa lekanyetsoang.
usage_example.english: ...for a covenant to a time unmeasured (everlasting).

senses.definition_en: The state of having undergone the ritual cutting of the foreskin.

usage_example.sesotho: E mong le e mong e motona ho lōna a bolotsoe.
usage_example.english: Every male among you shall be circumcised.

senses.definition_en: Minor rulers or tribal chiefs; the twelve leaders from Ishmael's line.

usage_example.sesotho: Ka sebele o tla hlahisa marenana a leshome le metso e ’meli.
usage_example.english: He shall beget twelve princes.

senses.definition_en: Large, leafy trees providing shade; specifically the Oaks of Mamre.

usage_example.sesotho: ...har’a lifate tse khōlō tsa Mamre.
usage_example.english: ...among the great trees of Mamre.

senses.definition_en: Finding grace or approval in the eyes of a superior.

usage_example.sesotho: ...haeba ke fumane kamohelo mahlong a hao.
usage_example.english: ...if I have found favor in your sight.

senses.definition_en: A loud cry or complaint reaching a judge regarding wickedness.

usage_example.sesotho: Mohoo oa pelaelo ka Sodoma...
usage_example.english: The outcry against Sodom...

senses.definition_en: Compassion that moves one to spare someone from punishment or harm.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka lebaka la qenehelo ea Jehova ho eena.
usage_example.english: ...because of the mercy of Jehovah toward him.

senses.definition_en: A standing stone or pillar; used here for the petrification of Lot's wife.

usage_example.sesotho: ...’me a fetoha sefika sa letsoai.
usage_example.english: ...and she became a pillar of salt.

senses.definition_en: A polite Sesotho idiom for sexual relations; literally 'to share the mats'.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e le hore re kopanele liphate le bona.
usage_example.english: ...that we may have sex with them.

senses.definition_en: Doing something with honest intent and a clear conscience.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke entse sena ka pelo e tšepahalang.
usage_example.english: I have done this in the integrity of my heart.

morphology.derivation: From 'rapela' (to pray) using the applied suffix '-ela'

senses.definition_en: The act of praying specifically for the benefit or healing of another person.

usage_example.sesotho: Abrahama a qala ho etsa thapeli ho Molimo oa ’nete.
usage_example.english: Abraham began to perform an intercession to the true God.

senses.definition_en: A symbolic 'covering' of a past offense; a gift that restores one's social standing.

usage_example.sesotho: Bona! ke lesira la mahlo bakeng sa bohle...
usage_example.english: Behold! it is a covering of the eyes for all...

senses.definition_en: The act of laughing; here it refers to both the joy of Isaac's birth and the irony of Sara's old age.

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo o ntokiselitse litšeho.
usage_example.english: God has prepared laughter for me.

senses.definition_en: The distance an arrow can travel when shot from a bow.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hoo e ka bang bohōle ba ho fula ka seqha.
usage_example.english: ...about the distance of a bowshot.

senses.definition_en: A solemn promise or statement of truth, often invoking God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hobane ka bobeli ba nkile kano moo.
usage_example.english: ...because both of them took an oath there.

senses.definition_en: The physical act of preparing wood for a fire by splitting it with a tool.

usage_example.sesotho: ...eaba o ratha patsi bakeng sa nyehelo.
usage_example.english: ...and he split the wood for the offering.

senses.definition_en: The act of providing or preparing what is necessary beforehand.

usage_example.sesotho: Ho tla etsoa tokisetso thabeng ea Jehova.
usage_example.english: Provision will be made on the mountain of Jehovah.

senses.definition_en: The upper part of the leg; used here in a ritualistic oath-taking context regarding procreation and lineage.

usage_example.sesotho: ...beha letsoho la hao tlas’a serope sa ka.
usage_example.english: ...put your hand under my thigh.

senses.definition_en: To make a journey or endeavor successful or fruitful.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hore na ebe Jehova o atlehisitse leeto la hae.
usage_example.english: ...whether Jehovah had made his journey prosperous.

senses.definition_en: To engage in deep thought, contemplation, or prayer.

usage_example.sesotho: Isaka o ne a ntse a itsamaela e le hore a thuise.
usage_example.english: Isaac was walking in order to meditate.

senses.definition_en: A title for God (El Shaddai) emphasizing His self-sufficiency and power to bless.

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo ea Matla ’Ohle o tla u hlohonolofatsa.
usage_example.english: May God Almighty bless you.

senses.definition_en: To use something (specifically a stone in this context) as a support for the head during sleep.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a nka le leng la majoe... a le sama.
usage_example.english: ...he took one of the stones... and put it at his head.

senses.definition_en: Evoking fear, respect, or intense wonder; grand and solemn.

usage_example.sesotho: Sebaka see se tšabeha hakaakang!
usage_example.english: How awesome is this place!

senses.definition_en: One-tenth of one's possessions or income dedicated for sacred use.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ruri ke tla u fa karolo ea lona ea leshome.
usage_example.english: ...I will surely give a tenth of it to You.

senses.definition_en: Refers to 'Covenant Loyalty' (Hebrew: Hesed); God's faithful, active love.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha ke tšoaneloe ke mosa oohle o lerato.
usage_example.english: I am not worthy of all the loving-kindness.

morphology.derivation: Diminutive of 'morena' (king/lord), implying a local ruler

senses.definition_en: A local leader or son of a king who holds authority over a small territory.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Shikeme... morenana oa naha.
usage_example.english: ...Shechem... prince of the country.

senses.definition_en: To make someone ritually or morally unclean; to ruin a person's reputation or purity.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hobane a silafalitse khaitseli ea bona.
usage_example.english: ...because he had defiled their sister.

senses.definition_en: To experience deep emotional distress or sorrow.

usage_example.sesotho: banna bana ba utloa bohloko ’me ba halefa.
usage_example.english: these men were grieved and very angry.

senses.definition_en: To engage in buying and selling; to conduct business in a land.

usage_example.sesotho: Lulang le hoebe ho eona.
usage_example.english: Dwell and trade in it.

senses.definition_en: A state of distress, social unrest, or danger brought upon a household.

usage_example.sesotho: Le ntliselitse khathatso.
usage_example.english: You have brought me trouble.

senses.definition_en: Idols or representations of deities other than the God of Israel.

usage_example.sesotho: Lahlang melimo esele e har’a lōna.
usage_example.english: Put away the foreign gods that are among you.

senses.definition_en: A supernatural dread or awe that prevents enemies from attacking.

usage_example.sesotho: ...tšabo e tsoang ho Molimo ea e-ba metseng.
usage_example.english: ...the terror of God was upon the cities.

senses.definition_en: To give birth to a child; the process of labor.

usage_example.sesotho: Ragele a beleha, ’me o ne a thatafalloa...
usage_example.english: Rachel labored in childbirth, and she had hard labor.

morphology.derivation: Noun meaning wind, spirit, or life-breath

senses.definition_en: The life force of a person; here, it refers to the moment of death.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha moea oa hae o tsoa (hobane o ile a shoa).
usage_example.english: ...as her soul was departing (for she died).

senses.definition_en: To be content or complete; used to describe Isaka's long and full life.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a tsofetse ’me a khotsofetse ke matsatsi.
usage_example.english: ...being old and full of days.

senses.definition_en: Accumulated property, livestock, and riches that define a family's status.

usage_example.sesotho: ...leruo lohle la hae, leo a le bokeletseng.
usage_example.english: ...all his goods which he had gained.

senses.definition_en: An uninhabited, dry, or barren region.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ea fumaneng liliba tsa metsi a chesang lefeelleng.
usage_example.english: ...who found the water in the wilderness.

senses.definition_en: To hold royal authority or exercise control over a country.

usage_example.sesotho: ...marena a busitseng naheng ea Edomo.
usage_example.english: ...the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.

senses.definition_en: Specific locations or territories where a group of people lives permanently.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho ea ka libaka tsa bona tsa bolulo.
usage_example.english: ...according to their dwelling places.

senses.definition_en: An account given to an authority figure about the misconduct or failures of others.

usage_example.sesotho: Josefa a tlisa tlaleho e mpe ka bona ho ntat’a bona.
usage_example.english: Joseph brought a bad report of them to his father.

senses.definition_en: To express sharp disapproval or criticism of someone because of their behavior or words.

usage_example.sesotho: ...nttat’ae a qala ho mo khalemela ka matla.
usage_example.english: ...his father rebuked him sharply.

senses.definition_en: People who buy and sell goods for profit, often traveling long distances in caravans.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale banna, bahoebi ba Bamidiane, ba feta.
usage_example.english: Then Midianite traders passed by.

senses.definition_en: To examine something to determine its identity or condition.

usage_example.sesotho: A qala ho se hlahloba ’me a hooa...
usage_example.english: He recognized it and cried out...

senses.definition_en: The state or period of being a widow; characterized by specific 'liaparo' (garments).

usage_example.sesotho: A hlobola liaparo tsa bohlolohali ba hae.
usage_example.english: She took off her widow's garments.

morphology.derivation: Noun for a walking stick or defensive rod

senses.definition_en: A stick carried by a person, often used by shepherds or as a symbol of authority.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le molamu o letsohong la hao.
usage_example.english: ...and the staff that is in your hand.

senses.definition_en: To be in the right or to have acted more justly than another in a specific situation.

usage_example.sesotho: O lokile ho mpheta.
usage_example.english: She has been more righteous than I.

morphology.derivation: Plural noun for two children born at the same time

senses.definition_en: Two offspring produced in the same pregnancy.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho ne ho e-na le mafahla ka mpeng ea hae.
usage_example.english: ...there were twins in her womb.

senses.definition_en: To cause someone or something to be successful or to flourish.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova o ne a e-na le Josefa ’me a atlehisa seo a se etsang.
usage_example.english: The LORD was with Joseph and made whatever he did prosper.

senses.definition_en: To decline to do something or to say no to a request.

usage_example.sesotho: Empa a hana eaba o re ho mosali oa mong’a hae...
usage_example.english: But he refused and said to his master's wife...

morphology.derivation: The chief controller or head manager

senses.definition_en: The official in charge of a prison and its inmates.

usage_example.sesotho: ...kamohelo mahlong a molaoli ea ka sehloohong oa ntlo ea chankana.
usage_example.english: ...favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

senses.definition_en: The action of explaining the meaning of something, especially a dream or a text.

usage_example.sesotho: Tlhaloso ea eona ke ena: Makala a mararo ke matsatsi a mararo.
usage_example.english: This is its interpretation: The three branches are three days.

senses.definition_en: A dark, underground prison cell.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba lokelang ho nkenya ka sekoting sa chankana.
usage_example.english: ...that they should put me into the dungeon.

senses.definition_en: To produce buds or flowers; a sign of health and productivity in the vine.

usage_example.sesotho: ...se ne se hlōmela letlōbō.
usage_example.english: ...it was as though it budded.

senses.definition_en: To extract juice by applying pressure.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka nka morara ke o tlhotlela ka har’a senoelo.
usage_example.english: ...I took the grapes and pressed them into the cup.

senses.definition_en: To fail to remember; to neglect a promise or a person.

usage_example.sesotho: ...mookameli oa baqhatsetsi ha aa ka a hopola Josefa ’me a mo lebala.
usage_example.english: ...the chief butler did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

senses.definition_en: Having or showing good judgment and the ability to act cautiously.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Faro a ke a batle monna ea masene le ea bohlale.
usage_example.english: ...let Pharaoh look for a man discerning and wise.

senses.definition_en: To bring together a large amount of resources over time.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba ke ba bokelle lijo tsa lilemo tsena tse tlang.
usage_example.english: Let them gather the food of these coming years.

senses.definition_en: High-quality fabric made from flax, worn by Egyptian royalty and priests.

usage_example.sesotho: ...o mo apesa liaparo tsa line ea boleng bo botle.
usage_example.english: ...clothed him in garments of fine linen.

senses.definition_en: Producing many offspring or results; to be made productive.

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo o nkatisitse naheng ea ho sohlokeha ha ka.
usage_example.english: God has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

morphology.derivation: Plural noun for grain storage structures

senses.definition_en: Buildings designed specifically to keep grain safe from moisture and pests.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Josefa a qala ho bula meliko eohle ea lijo-thollo.
usage_example.english: ...Joseph began to open all the storehouses of grain.

senses.definition_en: To bend the body forward and downward as a sign of respect or submission.

usage_example.sesotho: ...barab’abo Josefa ba tla ’me ba mo inamela.
usage_example.english: ...Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to him.

senses.definition_en: Being truthful and of good character; not deceptive.

usage_example.sesotho: Re banna ba lokileng. Bahlanka ba hao ha se lihloela.
usage_example.english: We are honest men. Your servants are not spies.

senses.definition_en: Severe mental or physical pain; deep suffering.

usage_example.sesotho: ...re bone mahlomola a moea oa hae...
usage_example.english: ...we saw the anguish of his soul...

morphology.derivation: Noun for food prepared for a journey

senses.definition_en: Supplies of food and water specifically for a trip or travel.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le ho ba fa mofaho bakeng sa tsela.
usage_example.english: ...and to give them provisions for the road.

senses.definition_en: To take someone away from a person, especially by death or separation.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke ’na eo le mo amohileng bana!
usage_example.english: It is I whom you have bereaved of children!

senses.definition_en: To give a solemn or strong warning; to testify with authority.

usage_example.sesotho: Monna eo o re paketse ka ho hlaka...
usage_example.english: The man solemnly warned us clearly...

senses.definition_en: To kill an animal specifically for food preparation.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u hlabe liphoofolo ’me u lokise.
usage_example.english: ...slaughter animals and prepare.

senses.definition_en: A feeling of great surprise or amazement.

usage_example.sesotho: ...banna bana ba ’na ba shebana ka ho makala.
usage_example.english: ...these men kept looking at each other in astonishment.

senses.definition_en: To hold oneself back; to exercise self-control over one's emotions.

usage_example.sesotho: ...eaba oa itšoara o re: 'Tšolang lijo.'
usage_example.english: ...then he restrained himself and said: 'Serve the bread.'

senses.definition_en: To catch up with someone who is traveling ahead.

usage_example.sesotho: Lelekisa banna bao ’me ruri u ba fihlele...
usage_example.english: Chase those men and indeed reach them...

senses.definition_en: To interpret omens or signs with professional or supernatural skill.

usage_example.sesotho: ...motho ea kang ’na a ka hlalosa ka botsebi lipontšo tsa se tlang?
usage_example.english: ...could a man such as I expertly explain the signs of what is coming?

senses.definition_en: To be violently ripped apart, usually by a wild animal.

usage_example.sesotho: Oe, ruri o rusolotsoe!
usage_example.english: Alas, surely he is torn to pieces!

senses.definition_en: Deep distress caused by loss or disappointment.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le tla theolela moriri oa ka o moputsoa ka mesarelo Sheole.
usage_example.english: ...you will bring down my gray hair with sorrow to Sheol.

senses.definition_en: To be so overwhelmed with shock or fear that one is unable to act or speak.

usage_example.sesotho: ...barab’abo ba ne ba sa khone ho mo araba... hobane o ne a ba ferekantse.
usage_example.english: ...his brothers could not answer him... because he had dismayed them.

senses.definition_en: The action of being rescued or set free from danger or starvation.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho bolokoe le phela ka ho pholosoa ho hoholo.
usage_example.english: ...to keep you alive by a great deliverance.

morphology.derivation: Stative/Neuter form denoting a state of being poor

senses.definition_en: To fall into a state of having little or no money or food.

usage_example.sesotho: ...esere uena le ba ntlo ea hao... la futsaneha.
usage_example.english: ...lest you and your household... come to poverty.

senses.definition_en: The best, most productive, and richest resources of a country.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le je karolo e nonneng ea naha.
usage_example.english: ...and you will eat the fat/rich part of the land.

morphology.derivation: Verb describing a sudden return of vitality

senses.definition_en: To come back to life or regain one's spirit after a period of numbness or depression.

usage_example.sesotho: ...moea oa ntat’a bona Jakobo oa qala ho hlasimoloha.
usage_example.english: ...the spirit of their father Jacob began to revive.

senses.definition_en: A term used in censuses to count individual human beings; souls.

usage_example.sesotho: ...meea eohle e ne e le mashome a supileng.
usage_example.english: ...all the persons/souls were seventy.

senses.definition_en: To make something or oneself ready for a specific purpose or journey.

usage_example.sesotho: Josefa a lokisa koloi ea hae...
usage_example.english: Joseph prepared/made ready his chariot...

morphology.derivation: Reduplicated form of 'great/elder' for emphasis on lineage

senses.definition_en: Forefathers; people from whom one is descended, usually more remote than grandparents.

usage_example.sesotho: ...rōna hammoho le baholo-holo ba rōna...
usage_example.english: ...we together with our ancestors...

morphology.derivation: Noun for 'liver' or 'courage', used here for capability

senses.definition_en: Possessing the skill, courage, or strength to perform a task well.

usage_example.sesotho: ...haeba u tseba hore har’a bona ho na le banna ba sebete...
usage_example.english: ...if you know that among them there are capable/brave men...

morphology.derivation: Intransitive verb denoting a state of extreme exhaustion

senses.definition_en: To become weak or fail in vigor; to be worn down by hardship or hunger.

usage_example.sesotho: ...naha ea Egepeta le naha ea Kanana tsa phophotheha ka lebaka la tlala.
usage_example.english: ...the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine.

morphology.derivation: Noun from verb 'fapanyetsana' (to exchange with each other)

senses.definition_en: The act of giving one thing and receiving another in return.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a ’na a ba fa bohobe e le phapanyetsano bakeng sa lipere...
usage_example.english: ...he kept giving them bread as an exchange for horses...

senses.definition_en: A formal rule or regulation established by an authority.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Josefa o ho etsa molao-taelo ho fihlela letsatsing lena...
usage_example.english: Then Joseph made it a law/decree until this day...

morphology.derivation: Applied form of 'hlapanya' (to swear an oath to someone)

senses.definition_en: To make a solemn statement or promise calling on a divine witness.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba o re: 'Ntlhapanyetse.' Kahoo a mo hlapanyetsa.
usage_example.english: Then he said: 'Swear to me.' So he swore to him.

senses.definition_en: A vast assembly or group of different peoples or tribes.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke tla u fetola phutheho ea lichaba...
usage_example.english: ...I will make you a multitude/assembly of nations...

morphology.derivation: Noun from verb 'fa' (to give); that which is given to an heir

senses.definition_en: Property, titles, or rights passed on to a descendant after death.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba tla bitsetsoa lefeng la bona...
usage_example.english: They will be called by their inheritance...

morphology.derivation: To pull out of a difficult state or debt

senses.definition_en: To release from blame, debt, or distress; to rescue from a negative situation.

usage_example.sesotho: Lengeloi le ’nileng la ntopolla tlokotsing eohle...
usage_example.english: The Angel who has redeemed me from all evil/calamity...

senses.definition_en: To fail to satisfy or to cause mild annoyance or disagreement.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha hoa ka ha mo khahlisa...
usage_example.english: ...it did not please him (he was displeased)...

senses.definition_en: Weapons representing military conquest and strength.

usage_example.sesotho: ...seo ke se nkileng... ka sabole ea ka le ka seqha sa ka.
usage_example.english: ...that which I took... by my sword and by my bow.

senses.definition_en: A prophetic term referring to the future destiny or the final period of a sequence.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke le bolelle se tla le etsahalla karolong e qetellang ea matsatsi.
usage_example.english: ...let me tell you what will happen to you in the final part of the days.

morphology.derivation: Abstract noun meaning excellence or decorative beauty

senses.definition_en: The quality of being worthy of honor or respect; high rank or excellence.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bokhabane bo hlomphehang le bokhabane ba matla.
usage_example.english: ...the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power.

senses.definition_en: A young lion, representing growing strength and royal potential.

usage_example.sesotho: Juda ke lelinyane la tau.
usage_example.english: Judah is a lion's whelp.

senses.definition_en: An ornamental staff carried by rulers on ceremonial occasions as a symbol of sovereignty.

usage_example.sesotho: Lere la borena le ke ke la sutha ho Juda...
usage_example.english: The scepter shall not depart from Judah...

morphology.derivation: Verb describing the predatory action of a wolf

senses.definition_en: To aggressively hunt and tear apart prey.

usage_example.sesotho: Benjamine o tla ’ne a rusolle joaloka phiri.
usage_example.english: Benjamin will keep on tearing/ravening like a wolf.

senses.definition_en: Professionals skilled in medicine and, in this context, the Egyptian art of mummification.

usage_example.sesotho: Josefa a laela bahlanka ba hae, lingaka, hore li tlotse setopo...
usage_example.english: Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm the body...

morphology.derivation: From 'otla' (to beat/strike), where grain is beaten

senses.definition_en: A hard, level surface where grain is separated from the straw; often used as a gathering place.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba fihla seotlong sa Atade...
usage_example.english: They came to the threshing floor of Atad...

morphology.derivation: Causative form; to cause someone to be at peace/dry tears

senses.definition_en: To alleviate the grief or distress of someone.

usage_example.sesotho: Kahoo a ba tšelisa ’me a bua le bona ka mokhoa o khothatsang.
usage_example.english: So he comforted them and spoke to them in a reassuring/encouraging way.

morphology.derivation: To direct attention or care toward someone

senses.definition_en: A divine act where God intervenes in human affairs to fulfill a promise or rescue.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ruri Molimo o tla lebisa tlhokomelo ea hae ho lōna...
usage_example.english: ...surely God will visit you / pay attention to you...

morphology.derivation: To become many; to increase in quantity

senses.definition_en: To increase greatly in number; to proliferate rapidly.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba qala ho ngatafala; ba ’na ba ata...
usage_example.english: ...they began to multiply; they continued to spread...

senses.definition_en: Fortified cities used for storing grain, weapons, or trade goods.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba qala ho haha metse e le libaka tsa polokelo...
usage_example.english: ...they began to build cities as places of storage...

morphology.derivation: Mud or wet clay used in construction

senses.definition_en: A mixture of lime, sand, and water, or simply wet mud, used to bond bricks together.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka ho etsa seretse sa letsopa le litene...
usage_example.english: ...by making clay mortar and bricks...

senses.definition_en: Healthy, strong, and capable of quick action (specifically regarding labor and birth).

usage_example.sesotho: ...Kahobane ba tletse bophelo, ba beleha le pele...
usage_example.english: ...Because they are lively/vigorous, they give birth before...

senses.definition_en: Young children or newborns.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Ke bana ba bona ba banyenyane feela...
usage_example.english: ...It was only their little ones...

morphology.derivation: A water plant used for making paper and baskets

senses.definition_en: Reeds or stalks of the papyrus plant commonly found along the Nile.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a mo nkela areka ea loli...
usage_example.english: ...she took for him an ark of bulrushes...

senses.definition_en: Payment given for work or services rendered.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke tla u fa moputso oa hao.
usage_example.english: ...I will give you your wages.

senses.definition_en: A heavy load; figuratively, the difficult life of slavery.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hore a talime moroalo oo ba o jereng...
usage_example.english: ...that he might look at the burdens they were bearing...

morphology.derivation: Plural from 'noa' (to drink); place for drinking

senses.definition_en: Long, shallow containers used for providing water to livestock.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba tlatsa linoelo hore ba noese mohlape...
usage_example.english: ...they filled the troughs to water the flock...

morphology.derivation: Infinitve used as a noun for deep sound of pain

senses.definition_en: Deep, inarticulate sounds expressing pain, grief, or fatigue.

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo a utloa ho bobola ha bona...
usage_example.english: God heard their groaning...

senses.definition_en: An uncultivated, uninhabited region; a wasteland.

usage_example.sesotho: ...khannela mohlape ka bophirimela ho lefeella...
usage_example.english: ...driving the flock to the west of the desert...

morphology.derivation: Plural noun from verb meaning to cause to suffer/wither

senses.definition_en: A state of pain, distress, or grief.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke bone mahloreho a sechaba sa ka...
usage_example.english: ...I have seen the affliction/sorrows of my people...

senses.definition_en: An act of offering something to a deity.

usage_example.sesotho: ...re batla ho etsetsa Jehova Molimo oa rōna sehlabelo.
usage_example.english: ...we want to make a sacrifice to the LORD our God.

morphology.derivation: Acts that cause one to be 'amazed' or 'stunned'

senses.definition_en: Miraculous acts that demonstrate divine power.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka liketso tsa ka tsohle tse hlollang...
usage_example.english: ...with all my wonders/amazing acts...

senses.definition_en: Fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha ke motho ea buang ka mokhoa o phollatsi...
usage_example.english: ...I am not a person who speaks in an eloquent way...

morphology.derivation: From 'nganga' (to argue/resist); state of being unyielding

senses.definition_en: Unreasonably determined to have one's own way; obstinate.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke tla tlohela pelo ea hae hore e be manganga...
usage_example.english: ...I will let his heart be stubborn/hardened...

senses.definition_en: The act of prostrating oneself as a sign of deep reverence or worship.

usage_example.sesotho: ...joale sa inama ’me sa itihela fatše ka lifahleho.
usage_example.english: ...then they bowed and threw themselves down on their faces.

morphology.derivation: A 'falling' sickness that spreads to many

senses.definition_en: A fatal epidemic disease.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a ka re otla ka lefu la seoa kapa ka sabole.
usage_example.english: ...He might strike us with pestilence or with the sword.

morphology.derivation: Plural; the cut stalks of grain left in the ground

senses.definition_en: The cut stalks of cereal plants left in the ground after harvesting.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho bokella litlhaka bakeng sa joang.
usage_example.english: ...to gather stubble instead of straw.

senses.definition_en: Deceptive or groundless statements.

usage_example.sesotho: ...se se ke sa ela hloko mantsoe a bohata.
usage_example.english: ...let them not pay attention to false words.

morphology.derivation: A state of being perplexed or in a difficult position

senses.definition_en: A state of great difficulty, danger, or misfortune.

usage_example.sesotho: ...balaoli ba bara ba Iseraele ba ipona ba le tsietsing e mpe...
usage_example.english: ...the officers of the sons of Israel saw they were in bad trouble...

morphology.derivation: Symbol of active divine intervention and power

senses.definition_en: A metaphor for God's manifest power and his direct action in the world.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ruri ke tla le pholosa ka letsoho le otlolohileng...
usage_example.english: ...surely I will rescue you with an outstretched arm...

morphology.derivation: Infinitve used as noun for losing heart or hope

senses.definition_en: A loss of courage or hope; a state of deep depression caused by hardship.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ha baa ka ba mamela Moshe ka lebaka la ho nyahama...
usage_example.english: ...they did not listen to Moses because of discouragement...

senses.definition_en: Living in a place that is not one's native home; a temporary stay.

usage_example.sesotho: ...naha ea bojaki ba bona...
usage_example.english: ...the land of their pilgrimage/sojourning...

morphology.derivation: Plural noun referring to ancestral lines or biological family groups

senses.definition_en: The lines of descent of a person or family.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho ea ka masika a bona...
usage_example.english: ...according to their generations/lineage...

senses.definition_en: An extraordinary event manifesting divine intervention in human affairs.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Itlhahisetseng mohlolo...
usage_example.english: ...Show a miracle for yourselves...

morphology.derivation: Plural of 'moloi'; those who practice magic/sorcery

senses.definition_en: Persons who claim or are believed to have magic powers.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Faro le eena a bitsa banna ba bohlale le baloi...
usage_example.english: ...Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers...

senses.definition_en: Occult knowledge or rituals used to produce supernatural effects.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba qala ho etsa ntho e tšoanang ka tsebo ea bona ea sephiri...
usage_example.english: ...they began to do the same thing by their secret knowledge...

morphology.derivation: Diminutive plural for small rivers or irrigation channels

senses.definition_en: Small rivers or man-made irrigation channels branching from a main river.

usage_example.sesotho: ...holim’a melatsoana ea Nile...
usage_example.english: ...over the streams of the Nile...

morphology.derivation: To be filled with a crawling or moving mass

senses.definition_en: To be present in large numbers, typically referring to insects or small animals.

usage_example.sesotho: Nōka ea Nile e tla nyeunya lihoho...
usage_example.english: The Nile river will swarm with frogs...

senses.definition_en: Large amounts of items piled on top of each other.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba ba qala ho li bokella, e le liqubu-qubu...
usage_example.english: Then they began to gather them, as heaps...

senses.definition_en: To treat as different or to separate for a specific purpose.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke tla etsa hore naha ea Goshene... e khethollehe...
usage_example.english: ...I will make the land of Goshen... be set apart...

senses.definition_en: Small parasitic insects or flying gnats.

usage_example.sesotho: ...lerōle lohle la lefatše la fetoha menoang...
usage_example.english: ...all the dust of the earth turned into gnats...

morphology.derivation: From 'bopa' (to mold/shape); where bricks or pottery are fired

senses.definition_en: An enclosed structure in which material is heated to very high temperatures.

usage_example.sesotho: Inkeleng mosili oa sebōpi...
usage_example.english: Take for yourselves ashes of a furnace...

senses.definition_en: A loud rumbling or crashing noise heard after a lightning flash.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Jehova a hlahisa lialuma le sefako...
usage_example.english: ...Jehovah produced thunder and hail...

morphology.derivation: To beat or strike repeatedly and violently

senses.definition_en: To strike something with heavy blows, causing destruction.

usage_example.sesotho: ...’me sa ruthutha mefuta eohle ea lifate tsa naha.
usage_example.english: ...and it shattered all kinds of trees of the field.

senses.definition_en: The part of something that remains after the rest has been taken or destroyed.

usage_example.sesotho: ...li tla ja sohle se phonyohileng, seo le se sietsoeng ke sefako...
usage_example.english: ...they shall eat the residue of what is left, which remains to you from the hail...

senses.definition_en: Adult men who are physically strong and fit for labor or war.

usage_example.sesotho: ...tsamaeang lōna banna ba shahlileng...
usage_example.english: ...go now, you who are men...

morphology.derivation: From 'chesa' (to burn); offerings that are completely consumed by fire

senses.definition_en: Sacrifices where the animal is entirely consumed by fire on an altar.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u tla re fa matsohong mahlabelo le linyehelo tsa secheso...
usage_example.english: ...you must give us sacrifices and burnt offerings...

morphology.derivation: The keratinous tip of a toe of an ungulate mammal

senses.definition_en: The horny part of the foot of an animal like a cow, horse, or sheep.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha ho khōla e tla lumelloa ho sala...
usage_example.english: Not a hoof shall be left behind...

morphology.derivation: Idiomatic: 'In the belly of the night'

senses.definition_en: Twelve o'clock at night; the middle of the night.

usage_example.sesotho: Hoo e ka bang har’a mp’a bosiu ke tla tsoela bohareng ba Egepeta.
usage_example.english: About midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt.

morphology.derivation: The one who opens the womb

senses.definition_en: The first child born to a particular person or couple.

usage_example.sesotho: ...letsibolo le leng le le leng naheng ea Egepeta le tla shoa...
usage_example.english: ...every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die...

senses.definition_en: Bread made without yeast or any raising agent, typically flat.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba lokela ho e ja... le mahobe a sa lomosoang...
usage_example.english: ...they must eat it... with unleavened bread...

morphology.derivation: From Afrikaans 'kosyn'; the vertical side-pieces of a door frame

senses.definition_en: The two vertical posts of a door frame.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba a qaphaletse likoseneng tse peli tsa monyako...
usage_example.english: ...put it on the two doorposts...

morphology.derivation: Idiomatic for the period between sunset and total darkness

senses.definition_en: The period of evening light between sunset and full darkness.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e tla e hlaba pakeng tsa lishoalane tse peli.
usage_example.english: ...shall kill it at twilight.

morphology.derivation: From 'jaka' (to live in a foreign place)

senses.definition_en: A temporary stay in a place where one is not a native.

usage_example.sesotho: Nako ea ho lula ha bara ba Iseraele...
usage_example.english: The time of the sojourn of the children of Israel...

morphology.derivation: The state of being a servant or slave (lekhoba)

senses.definition_en: The state of being a slave; involuntary servitude.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le tsoileng Egepeta, ntlong ea makhoba...
usage_example.english: ...you came out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage...

morphology.derivation: Causative form: 'to make walk' or 'to guide'

senses.definition_en: To show the way to a destination by going in front of or beside.

usage_example.sesotho: ...topallo ea leru ho ba tsamaisa tseleng...
usage_example.english: ...a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way...

morphology.derivation: Descriptive: 'a band worn on the forehead'

senses.definition_en: Small leather boxes containing Hebrew texts, worn on the forehead and arm during prayer.

usage_example.sesotho: E tla ba... lebanta le roaloang phatleng pakeng tsa mahlo a hao...
usage_example.english: It shall be... as frontlets between your eyes...

senses.definition_en: To follow someone or something in order to catch or attack them.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka sebele o tla ba lelekisa ’me ke tla itlotlisa ka Faro...
usage_example.english: ...he will surely pursue them and I will gain glory through Pharaoh...

morphology.derivation: A vertical structure that defines or encloses an area

senses.definition_en: A continuous vertical brick or stone structure; used here metaphorically for the standing water.

usage_example.sesotho: ...metsi e le lebota ho bona ka letsohong la bona le letona...
usage_example.english: ...the waters were a wall to them on their right hand...

senses.definition_en: Land that is free from water or moisture.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le ho fetola boliba ba leoatle mobu o omileng...
usage_example.english: ...and to turn the depths of the sea into dry ground...

morphology.derivation: Applied form of 'liha' (to cause to fall)

senses.definition_en: To remove from power or to throw down into a place.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Jehova a lihela Baegepeta ka har’a leoatle.
usage_example.english: ...Jehovah overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

senses.definition_en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good; majesty.

usage_example.sesotho: Ka bophahamo ba hao bo boholo u ka liha ba u tsohelang matla...
usage_example.english: In the greatness of your excellence you have overthrown those who rose against you...

senses.definition_en: To complain in a low, muttering way; to show discontent.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba batho ba qala ho korotlela Moshe...
usage_example.english: And the people began to complain against Moses...

morphology.derivation: Causative form: 'to cause to get well'

senses.definition_en: To make sound or whole; to restore to health.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hobane ke ’na Jehova ea le folisang.
usage_example.english: ...for I am Jehovah who heals you.

morphology.derivation: Iterative form: 'to pick up many things one by one'

senses.definition_en: To collect things from the ground; to glean.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba ne ba bo thonaka hoseng ho hong le ho hong...
usage_example.english: They gathered it every morning...

senses.definition_en: A day of religious observance and abstinence from work.

usage_example.sesotho: Hosasane ho tla bolokoa sabatha ea sabatha e halalelang...
usage_example.english: Tomorrow is a Sabbath rest, a holy Sabbath...

senses.definition_en: To become liquid by heat.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha letsatsi le chesa, bo ne bo qhibiliha.
usage_example.english: When the sun became hot, it melted.

senses.definition_en: Larvae of insects, especially those found in decaying matter.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bo ne bo tsoa libōkō ’me bo nkha hampe...
usage_example.english: ...it bred worms and stank...

morphology.derivation: To throw stones at someone with intent to kill or injure.

senses.definition_en: To attack or kill by throwing stones.

usage_example.sesotho: Ho se ho se hokae ’me se tla ntlepetsa ka majoe!
usage_example.english: They are almost ready to stone me!

morphology.derivation: Causative/Applied form: 'to cause to be supported'

senses.definition_en: To hold up or keep from falling.

usage_example.sesotho: Arone le Hure ba tšehetsa matsoho a hae...
usage_example.english: Aaron and Hur supported his hands...

senses.definition_en: Something that serves to preserve the memory of a person or an event.

usage_example.sesotho: Ngola sena e le sehopotso bukeng...
usage_example.english: Write this for a memorial in the book...

morphology.derivation: To give guidance or a suggestion for a course of action.

senses.definition_en: To offer suggestions about the best course of action to someone.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale mamela lentsoe la ka. Ke tla u eletsa...
usage_example.english: Now listen to my voice. I will advise you...

senses.definition_en: People in charge of a specific group; administrators.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u ba behe hore ba se okamele e le balaoli ba ba likete...
usage_example.english: ...place such over them to be rulers of thousands...

senses.definition_en: Severe suffering or privation; difficulties encountered during a journey.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le litsietsi tsohle tse ba hlahetseng tseleng...
usage_example.english: ...and all the hardship that had come upon them on the way...

senses.definition_en: A metaphor for divine protection, strength, and swift rescue.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e le hore nka le jara ka mapheo a lintsu ka le tlisa ho ’na.
usage_example.english: ...how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself.

senses.definition_en: A nation where every member has access to God and serves a mediatory role.

usage_example.sesotho: Le tla fetoha ’muso oa baprista le sechaba se halalelang ho ’na.
usage_example.english: And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.

morphology.derivation: To force a way through a barrier or crowd.

senses.definition_en: To push past a boundary or limit, often with curiosity or aggression.

usage_example.sesotho: ...hore se se ke sa leka ho phunyeletsa ho ea ho Jehova...
usage_example.english: ...lest they break through to gaze at the LORD...

senses.definition_en: The requirement of total and singular loyalty to God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...’na Jehova Molimo oa hao ke Molimo ea batlang boinehelo bo khethehileng...
usage_example.english: ...I, Jehovah your God, am a God requiring exclusive devotion...

senses.definition_en: Treating something sacred as common or worthless; taking a name in vain.
sesotho_term: tsela eo e seng ea bohlokoa

usage_example.sesotho: U se ke ua sebelisa lebitso la Jehova... ka tsela eo e seng ea bohlokoa...
usage_example.english: You shall not use the name of Jehovah... in a way that is not important...

senses.definition_en: Giving untrue testimony in a legal or social context.

usage_example.sesotho: U se ke ua paka ka bohata ha u le paki khahlanong le oa heno.
usage_example.english: You shall not bear false witness as a witness against your fellow man.

senses.definition_en: Case laws or legal rulings that provide precedents for social justice.

usage_example.sesotho: Tsena ke liqeto tsa boahloli tseo u tla li beha ka pel’a bona.
usage_example.english: These are the judgments which you shall set before them.

morphology.derivation: To seize and carry off a person by force.

senses.definition_en: Abducting someone, typically for sale or ransom.

usage_example.sesotho: Ea koetelang motho ’me a mo rekisa... ruri o tla bolaoa.
usage_example.english: He who kidnaps a man and sells him... shall surely be put to death.

headword_english: A goring / To thrust with horn

senses.definition_en: The act of an animal attacking with its horns.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba poho e hlaba monna kapa mosali...
usage_example.english: If an ox gores a man or a woman...

morphology.derivation: Literally 'to break' or 'to crush'; used for breaking into a house.

senses.definition_en: To enter a premises forcibly, typically with the intent to steal.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba lesholu le fumanoa le thuha ’me le otloa le shoa...
usage_example.english: If the thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies...

morphology.derivation: To mislead or draw someone into an action through persuasion.

senses.definition_en: To attract by arousing hope or desire; to seduce.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale haeba monna a eka moroetsana ea sa lebeletsoang...
usage_example.english: Now if a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed...

morphology.derivation: In this context, financial 'offspring' or interest on a loan.

senses.definition_en: Money paid regularly at a particular rate for the use of money lent.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u se ke ua ba joaloka ea alimanang a batla tsoala ho eena.
usage_example.english: ...you shall not be like a moneylender to him; you shall not charge him interest.

morphology.derivation: From 'ho ea ka nģ'a e 'ngoe' (to go towards one side).

senses.definition_en: Unfair bias in favor of one person or group over another.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha e le ea tlaase, u se ke ua bontša leeme tsekong ea hae.
usage_example.english: You shall not show partiality to a poor man in his dispute.

morphology.derivation: Reflexive form: 'to cause oneself to be refreshed/rested'.

senses.definition_en: To recover strength or energy through rest.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e le hore poho... le mojaki ba ikhatholle.
usage_example.english: ...so that the ox... and the stranger may be refreshed.

senses.definition_en: Standing stones used in pagan worship which Israel was commanded to destroy.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ruri u heletse litšiea tsa bona tse halalelang.
usage_example.english: ...completely break down their sacred pillars.

senses.definition_en: The blood used to seal and sanctify the legal agreement between God and Israel.

usage_example.sesotho: Ana ke mali a selekane seo Jehova a se hlabileng le lōna...
usage_example.english: This is the blood of the covenant which Jehovah has made with you...

senses.definition_en: The stone slabs on which the Ten Commandments were inscribed by God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke batla ho u fa matlapa a lejoe le molao...
usage_example.english: ...I want to give you the tablets of stone and the law...

senses.definition_en: A vivid description of divine majesty that is both bright and dangerous.

usage_example.sesotho: ...pono ea khanya ea Jehova e ne e tšoana le mollo o timetsang...
usage_example.english: ...the sight of the glory of Jehovah was like a consuming fire...

senses.definition_en: A hard, dense wood from the acacia tree, known for its durability.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba etse Areka ea lehong la leoka...
usage_example.english: They shall make an ark of acacia wood...

senses.definition_en: Twelve loaves of bread set out in the Tabernacle as a symbol of God's provision and communion.

usage_example.sesotho: U behe bohobe ba pontšo holim ’a tafole...
usage_example.english: And you shall set the showbread on the table...

morphology.derivation: A footprint or example to be followed.

senses.definition_en: The specific divine design or blueprint shown to Moses.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u li etsa ho latela mohlala oa tsona oo u ileng ua o bontšoa thabeng.
usage_example.english: ...make them according to the pattern which was shown you on the mountain.

senses.definition_en: Fasteners used to couple the curtain sets together to make 'one' tabernacle.

usage_example.sesotho: U etse lihakisi tse mashome a mahlano tsa khauta...
usage_example.english: And you shall make fifty gold clasps...

morphology.derivation: From 'ho sira' (to screen or to shade).

senses.definition_en: A heavy curtain that acted as a barrier to the most sacred area.

usage_example.sesotho: ...lesira le tla le etsetsa karohano pakeng tsa Sehalalelo le Sehalalelisiso.
usage_example.english: ...the veil shall be a divider for you between the Holy Place and the Most Holy.

morphology.derivation: Literally 'parts that fit in' or 'cough into' (fit snugly).

senses.definition_en: The projections at the end of a board designed to fit into a socket.

usage_example.sesotho: Foreimi ka 'ngoe e na le likarolo tse peli tse khohlelang...
usage_example.english: Each board shall have two tenons...

morphology.derivation: Plural of 'lenaka' (horn). Historically, grasping these horns provided sanctuary.

senses.definition_en: Four projections on the corners of the altar, often smeared with blood during rituals.

usage_example.sesotho: U etse manaka a eona likhutlong tsa eona tse ’nè.
usage_example.english: You shall make its horns on its four corners.

senses.definition_en: The metal used for all exterior Tabernacle items, symbolizing judgment or endurance.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u e koahele ka koporo.
usage_example.english: ...overlay it with bronze.

morphology.derivation: From 'ho thakhisa' (to pin down or to fasten).

senses.definition_en: The pegs used to anchor the courtyard curtains and the Tabernacle tent to the ground.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le lithakhisa tsohle tsa lebala ke tsa koporo.
usage_example.english: ...and all the pegs of the court shall be of bronze.

senses.definition_en: A sacred pouch worn by the High Priest to signify his role as a judge and representative of the tribes.

usage_example.sesotho: U etse kotla ea sefuba ea kahlolo e le mosebetsi oa mokhabisi...
usage_example.english: You shall make the breastplate of judgment, the work of a skillful workman...

morphology.derivation: Onomatopoeic from the sound of tinkling metal.

senses.definition_en: Small bells attached to the hem of the High Priest's robe.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le mangenengene a khauta pakeng tsa tsona ho potoloha.
usage_example.english: ...and bells of gold between them all around.

senses.definition_en: The style of engraving used for the stones and the gold plate, similar to a signet ring.
sesotho_term: mongolo o fatiloeng o kang oa tiiso

usage_example.sesotho: ...u ngole holim ’a lona ka mongolo o fatiloeng o kang oa tiiso...
usage_example.english: ...engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet...

morphology.derivation: Passive of 'tlatsa' (to fill). Literally to have one's hands filled with authority/sacrifice.

senses.definition_en: The formal installation of a person into the priestly office.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u ba tlotse u tlatse matsoho a bona ka matla u ba halaletse.
usage_example.english: ...anoint them, consecrate them, and fill their hands with power.

morphology.derivation: From 'ho tsukutla' (to shake or wave back and forth).

senses.definition_en: A specific ritual where the priest moved the offering in a waving motion.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u li tsukutle e le nyehelo e tsukutloang ka pel'a Jehova.
usage_example.english: ...and wave them as a wave offering before Jehovah.

senses.definition_en: The smoke of a sacrifice considered acceptable and aromatic to the deity.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke nyehelo e chesetsoang Jehova bakeng sa monko o thabisang.
usage_example.english: ...it is an offering made by fire to Jehovah for a soothing aroma.

morphology.derivation: Anatomical term for kidneys; often associated with inward emotions in Semitic thought.

senses.definition_en: Internal organs of the animal required for specific burnt offerings.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u nke lipshio tse peli le mafura a holim ’a tsona.
usage_example.english: ...take the two kidneys and the fat that is on them.

senses.definition_en: The act of officially installing someone into a sacred office.

usage_example.sesotho: ...kaha ke pheleu ea tlhomamiso.
usage_example.english: ...for it is a ram of consecration.

senses.definition_en: To cause a sacrifice to go up in smoke on an altar.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u etse hore li kubelle holim ’a aletare.
usage_example.english: ...and burn them (make them smoke) on the altar.

senses.definition_en: The refuse or intestinal waste of the sacrificial animal.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le bolokoe ba eona ka ntle ho liahelo.
usage_example.english: ...and its offal (dung) outside the camp.

senses.definition_en: A standard financial contribution required from all adults regardless of wealth.

usage_example.sesotho: Ea ruileng ha aa lokela ho ntša ho fetang halofo ea shekele.
usage_example.english: The rich shall not give more than half a shekel.

senses.definition_en: The penalty for violating the sanctity of the sacred oil or incense recipe.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ea tlotsang osele ka ’ona o tla felisoa sechabeng sa habo.
usage_example.english: ...whoever puts it on an outsider shall be cut off from his people.

senses.definition_en: A dry or liquid measure of approximately 3.6 to 5 liters.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le hine ea oli ea mohloaare.
usage_example.english: ...and a hin of olive oil.

morphology.derivation: To pound or grind with a mortar and pestle.

senses.definition_en: The process of grinding spices into a very fine dust for incense.
sesotho_term: ho tule hore e be phofo

usage_example.sesotho: U tule o mong oa oona hore e be phofo e thumisehileng.
usage_example.english: You shall beat some of it very fine (into powder).

senses.definition_en: Specially designed items requiring creative skill and planning.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bakeng sa ho qapa lisebelisoa, bakeng sa ho sebetsa ka khauta...
usage_example.english: ...to design artistic works, to work in gold...

morphology.derivation: Reversive form of 'hlompha' (to respect). To 'un-respect' or dishonor.

senses.definition_en: To violate the sanctity of something holy, specifically the Sabbath.

usage_example.sesotho: Ea e hlomphollang ruri o tla bolaoa.
usage_example.english: Everyone who profanes it (the Sabbath) shall surely be put to death.

morphology.derivation: Literal 'finger'. Metaphor for direct divine action.

senses.definition_en: A term signifying that the law was created directly by God's power without human intervention.

usage_example.sesotho: ...matlapa a lejoe a ngotsoeng ka monoana oa Molimo.
usage_example.english: ...tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.

senses.definition_en: Describing a people who refuse to bow or obey authority.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bona! ke sechaba se melala e sataletseng.
usage_example.english: ...indeed it is a stiff-necked people!

morphology.derivation: To wipe away or remove a mark/writing.

senses.definition_en: To remove someone's name from the book of life or a census record.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ka kōpo, u ntlhakole bukeng ea hao eo u e ngotseng.
usage_example.english: ...please, blot me out of Your book which You have written.

senses.definition_en: A state where people act without regard for laws or leaders.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Moshe o bona hore sechaba se tsoile taolong...
usage_example.english: ...Moses saw that the people were unrestrained (out of control)...

morphology.derivation: Generic term for a metal carving or shaping tool.

senses.definition_en: A technical tool used for detailed metalwork on the idol.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a e bōpa ka kofuto e betlang...
usage_example.english: ...he fashioned it with an engraving tool...

senses.definition_en: Direct and intimate communication without intermediaries.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a bua le Moshe lifahleho li talimane.
usage_example.english: The LORD spoke to Moses face to face.

morphology.derivation: The state of being 'there' or present.

senses.definition_en: The manifest presence of a deity among a people.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke tla tsamaea le uena ’me ka sebele ka u fa phomolo.
usage_example.english: My Presence will go with you and I will give you rest.

senses.definition_en: A natural hollow or opening in a rock face used for shelter.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ke u kenye mokoting oa lefika.
usage_example.english: ...I will put you in the cleft of the rock.

morphology.derivation: Common verb for carpentry or masonry.

senses.definition_en: The act of preparing stone tablets by cutting and smoothing them.

usage_example.sesotho: Ipetlele matlapa a mabeli a lejoe a tšoanang le a pele.
usage_example.english: Cut (carve) for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones.

morphology.derivation: Commonly used for the rays of the sun.

senses.definition_en: Visible light emanating from a person due to divine contact.

usage_example.sesotho: ...letlalo la sefahleho sa hae le ntša mahlaseli...
usage_example.english: ...the skin of his face shone (sent out rays)...

senses.definition_en: A divine attribute signifying God's intolerance of rivalry or idolatry.

usage_example.sesotho: ...Jehova, eo lebitso la hae e leng Poulelo, ke Molimo ea boulelang.
usage_example.english: ...the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

morphology.derivation: A specialized verb for textile production.

senses.definition_en: To draw out and twist fibers into thread or yarn.

usage_example.sesotho: Basali bohle ba nang le lipelo tse bohlale ba ohla ka matsoho.
usage_example.english: All the women who were gifted artisans spun yarn with their hands.

senses.definition_en: A contribution given out of personal desire rather than legal obligation.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bara ba Iseraele ba tlisetsa Jehova nyehelo ea boithatelo.
usage_example.english: ...the children of Israel brought a freewill offering to the LORD.

senses.definition_en: A person who creates the blueprints or artistic patterns for a project.

usage_example.sesotho: ...banna ba etsang mosebetsi le ho qapa lisebelisoa...
usage_example.english: ...men who do the work and those who design artistic works.

senses.definition_en: A projection on the end of a board designed to fit into a socket or mortise.

usage_example.sesotho: Foreimi ka 'ngoe e ne e e-na le likarolo tse peli tse khohlelang e 'ngoe ka har'a e 'ngoe.
usage_example.english: Each board had two tenons for binding one to another.

senses.definition_en: To command a stop to a specific activity, in this case, the bringing of gifts.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba sechaba se thibeloa ho e tlisa.
usage_example.english: And the people were restrained from bringing (more).

senses.definition_en: Metalwork shaped by hand striking rather than being poured into a mold.

usage_example.sesotho: A li etsa ka thepa e teiloeng ka hamore lintlheng tse peli.
usage_example.english: He made them of hammered work at the two ends.

morphology.derivation: Refers to a rounded or bulbous protrusion.

senses.definition_en: A rounded ornamental feature on the lampstand, resembling a flower bud.

usage_example.sesotho: Kotola e ka tlas’a makala a mabeli e ne e hlahella ho sona.
usage_example.english: A knob under the two branches was part of it.

senses.definition_en: To extend wings to their full width, usually for protection or flight.

usage_example.sesotho: ...likerubime tse peli tse phukalalitseng mapheo ho ea holimo.
usage_example.english: ...two cherubim spreading wings upward.

morphology.derivation: From 'ho thakhisa' (to nail or fasten down).

senses.definition_en: Metal or wooden pins used to anchor the tabernacle structure to the ground.

usage_example.sesotho: Lithakhisa tsohle tsa tente... e ne e le tsa koporo.
usage_example.english: All the tent pegs... were made of bronze.

senses.definition_en: A formal list or enumeration of materials used in a project.

usage_example.sesotho: Tse latelang ke lintho tse thathamisitsoeng tsa tabernakele.
usage_example.english: The following are the listed things (inventory) of the tabernacle.

senses.definition_en: Polished metal surfaces used for seeing one's reflection.

usage_example.sesotho: A etsa beisine... a sebelisa liipone tsa makhabunyane.
usage_example.english: He made the basin... using the mirrors of the women.

morphology.derivation: Onomatopoeic for the sound of tinkling metal.

senses.definition_en: Small gold instruments attached to the priest's robe that produce sound when he moves.

usage_example.sesotho: ba etsa mangenengene a khauta e hloekileng.
usage_example.english: they made bells of pure gold.

senses.definition_en: Fruit-shaped ornaments made of woven thread used to decorate the hem of the priestly robe.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba etsa mangenengene pakeng tsa likharenate.
usage_example.english: ...they put the bells between the pomegranates.

morphology.derivation: To gaze at or examine closely.

senses.definition_en: The act of evaluating work to ensure it meets specifications.

usage_example.sesotho: Moshe a talima mosebetsi oohle.
usage_example.english: Moses looked over all the work.

morphology.derivation: Commonly used for pitching a tent or setting up a pole.

senses.definition_en: The act of assembling and fixing a structure into its upright position.

usage_example.sesotho: ka la pele khoeling, u hlome tabernakele.
usage_example.english: on the first day of the month, you shall set up the tabernacle.

headword_english: To break camp / To pull up stakes

morphology.derivation: The reversive form of 'ho hloma' (to set up).

senses.definition_en: The act of dismantling a camp or tent to move to the next location.

usage_example.sesotho: ha leru le phahama... ba ne ba hlomolla liahelo.
usage_example.english: when the cloud rose... they would break camp.

senses.definition_en: The brilliant, visible manifestation of the divine presence.

usage_example.sesotho: khanya ea Jehova ea tlala tabernakele.
usage_example.english: the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.

senses.definition_en: To make amends or provide a covering for sins to restore a relationship with God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...bakeng sa hore a koahele libe tsa hae.
usage_example.english: ...for him to make atonement for his sins.

senses.definition_en: Free from physical defects, spots, or illnesses.

usage_example.sesotho: o lokela ho hlahisa e tona, e phetseng hantle.
usage_example.english: he should present a male, a healthy one (without blemish).

senses.definition_en: A vegetable-based offering consisting of flour, oil, and incense.

usage_example.sesotho: haeba moea o itseng o ka hlahisa nyehelo ea lijo-thollo...
usage_example.english: if a soul brings a grain offering...

senses.definition_en: The portion of an offering burned on the altar to represent the whole.

usage_example.sesotho: moprista... a etse hore e kubelle e le khopotso.
usage_example.english: the priest... shall burn it as a memorial.

senses.definition_en: A voluntary sacrifice representing peace and fellowship between God and man.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba nyehelo ea hae e le sehlabelo se kopanetsoeng...
usage_example.english: If his offering is a peace offering...

senses.definition_en: The richest part of the animal, reserved exclusively for God in sacrifices.

usage_example.sesotho: Mafura ’ohle ke a Jehova.
usage_example.english: All the fat is the LORD's.

morphology.derivation: Description of the specific anatomy of sheep.

senses.definition_en: The broad tail of certain sheep, removed entirely for the altar.

usage_example.sesotho: O tla tlosa mohatla oohle o mafura haufi le lesapo la mokokotlo.
usage_example.english: He shall remove the whole fat tail close to the backbone.

senses.definition_en: A transgression of the law committed without malicious intent or through ignorance.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba moea o etsa sebe ka phoso...
usage_example.english: If a soul sins by mistake...

senses.definition_en: A sacrifice for sins requiring restitution or compensation for a violation of rights.

usage_example.sesotho: o tlise nyehelo ea oona ea molato ho Jehova.
usage_example.english: he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD.

senses.definition_en: The verbal admission of a specific sin as a prerequisite for forgiveness.

usage_example.sesotho: joale o bolele hore na o entse sebe ka tsela efe.
usage_example.english: then he shall confess in what way he has sinned.

senses.definition_en: The act of making good on a loss or injury; paying back with interest.

usage_example.sesotho: O tla etsa puseletso bakeng sa sebe seo o se entseng.
usage_example.english: He shall make restitution for the sin he committed.

senses.definition_en: Something given to another person to be kept in safety; a security deposit.

usage_example.sesotho: ...kapa peheletso e seatleng sa oona.
usage_example.english: ...or about a deposit in his hand.

senses.definition_en: Something that occurs without stopping or interruption.

usage_example.sesotho: mollo o tla lula o tuka aletareng kamehla.
usage_example.english: the fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually.

senses.definition_en: A grade of holiness reserved for the sanctuary and specific portions of the sacrifices.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke ntho e halalelang ka ho fetisisa, joaloka nyehelo ea sebe.
usage_example.english: It is most holy, like the sin offering.

senses.definition_en: To be removed from the covenant community, either through death or exile.

usage_example.sesotho: moea o jang mali leha e le afe, moea oo o felisoe sechabeng.
usage_example.english: the soul that eats any blood, that soul shall be cut off from his people.

senses.definition_en: A state of ritual impurity that makes a sacrifice invalid.

usage_example.sesotho: E tla ba ntho e silafetseng, ’me moea o jang e ’ngoe ea eona o tla arabella phoso.
usage_example.english: It shall be an abomination, and the person who eats it shall bear his guilt.

senses.definition_en: The formal act of setting someone apart for a sacred role or office.

usage_example.sesotho: Ena e ne e le pheleu ea tlhomamiso.
usage_example.english: This was the ram of consecration.

senses.definition_en: Sacred lots kept in the High Priest's breastplate used to consult God's judgment.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a kenya Urime le Thummime ka har'a kotla ea sefuba.
usage_example.english: ...he put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastplate.

senses.definition_en: A linen head covering worn by the priests.

usage_example.sesotho: a mo roesa tuku hloohong.
usage_example.english: he put the turban on his head.

senses.definition_en: The majestic and visible manifestation of God's presence, often associated with light or cloud.

usage_example.sesotho: khanya ea Jehova ea bonahala ho sechaba sohle.
usage_example.english: the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.

headword_sesotho.orthographic: mollo oo e seng oa molao
headword_sesotho.tone_marked: mōllō ōō ē sēng ōā mōlāō

syllables.orthographic: mol-lo oo e seng oa mo-la-o

morphology.derivation: Mollo (fire) + negative relative clause (not of the law).

senses.definition_en: An unauthorized or illegitimate fire used in worship that violates God's specific commands.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba qala ho nyehela ka pel'a Jehova mollo oo e seng oa molao.
usage_example.english: ...they offered profane fire before the LORD.

senses.definition_en: To perceive a difference; to separate things into categories based on their nature.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e le hore ho khetholloe pakeng tsa ntho e halalelang le e silafetseng.
usage_example.english: ...that you may distinguish between holy and unholy.

morphology.derivation: To bring up food from the first stomach to chew it again.

senses.definition_en: A digestive process in ruminants; used here as a marker for ritual purity in land animals.

usage_example.sesotho: ...leha e le efe e busolosang har'a liphoofolo, le ka e ja.
usage_example.english: ...whatever among the animals chews the cud, you may eat.

senses.definition_en: Small, stiff plates growing out of the skin of a fish; a requirement for clean seafood.

usage_example.sesotho: Ntho e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe e nang le makhakhapha le ka e ja.
usage_example.english: Everything that has scales you may eat.

morphology.derivation: Negative relative form of 'hloeka' (to be clean).

senses.definition_en: Ritually impure; unfit for consumption or for entering the presence of God.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha ea hloeka bakeng sa lōna.
usage_example.english: It is unclean to you.

senses.definition_en: The state or process of becoming ritually clean after a period of impurity.

usage_example.sesotho: O tla lula maling a tlhoekiso ka matsatsi a mashome a mararo a metso e meraro.
usage_example.english: She shall then continue in the blood of her purification thirty-three days.

morphology.derivation: Often refers to various infectious skin diseases or molds.
