senses.definition_en: A ritual and physical impurity involving skin deterioration or spreading fungus in materials.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke lepera le siphohang lefatleng.
usage_example.english: It is leprosy breaking out on the bald head.

senses.definition_en: To set a person or object apart from the community to prevent contamination.

usage_example.sesotho: ...moprista a behelle ea nang le lefu leo ka thōko.
usage_example.english: ...the priest shall isolate the one who has the sore.

senses.definition_en: An aromatic plant used in purification rituals for sprinkling liquids.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a nke linonyana tse peli le lehong la kedare le hysopa.
usage_example.english: ...he shall take two birds and cedar wood and hyssop.

senses.definition_en: A persistent and destructive form of mold or disease that continues to spread despite treatment.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke lepera le bolaeang ka tlung.
usage_example.english: It is an active leprosy in the house.

senses.definition_en: The monthly ritual impurity of a woman; a state of being set apart for seven days.

usage_example.sesotho: ...e tla ba ea sa hloekang joaloka matsatsing a ho se hloeke nakong ea ha a ilela khoeli.
usage_example.english: ...she shall be unclean as in the days of her customary impurity.

senses.definition_en: A container made of fired clay, which must be broken if it becomes ritually contaminated.

usage_example.sesotho: Sejana leha e le sefe sa letsopa... se lokela ho thuhakanngoa.
usage_example.english: The vessel of earth... shall be broken.

senses.definition_en: The act of making amends for sin or error, specifically the ritual reconciliation between God and man.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho tla koaheloa libe bakeng sa lōna ho phatlalatsa hore le hloekile.
usage_example.english: ...on that day the priest shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you.

morphology.derivation: Transliterated from Hebrew, meaning 'goat of departure' or 'entire removal'.

senses.definition_en: The goat upon which the sins of the people were symbolically placed before it was sent into the wilderness.

usage_example.sesotho: ...pōli eo lotho e oetseng ho eona bakeng sa Azazele e lokela ho emisoa e phela.
usage_example.english: ...the goat on which the lot fell to be the scapegoat shall be presented alive.

senses.definition_en: The legal and spiritual responsibility for shedding life without divine authorization.

usage_example.sesotho: ...motho eo o tla balloa molato oa mali.
usage_example.english: ...bloodguilt shall be imputed to that man.

morphology.derivation: Can mean wind, spirit, or the life-force.

senses.definition_en: The vital principle or life-force contained within the blood of a living creature.

usage_example.sesotho: Etsoe moea oa nama o maling.
usage_example.english: For the life of the flesh is in the blood.

senses.definition_en: A Hebrew idiom referring to sexual intercourse, specifically in the context of forbidden or shameful acts.

usage_example.sesotho: U se ke ua apola bofeela ba mosali oa ntat’ao.
usage_example.english: The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover.

morphology.derivation: Borrowed from Hebrew 'Molekh', a Canaanite deity.

senses.definition_en: An ancient Canaanite god associated with child sacrifice through fire.

usage_example.sesotho: U se ke ua lumella hore ngoana leha e le ofe oa hao a neheloe ho Moloke.
usage_example.english: You shall not let any of your descendants pass through to Molech.

headword_sesotho.orthographic: u rate oa heno joalokaha u ithata
headword_sesotho.tone_marked: ū rātē ōā hēnō jōālōkāhā ū īthātā

syllables.orthographic: u ra-te oa he-no joa-lo-ka-ha u i-tha-ta

senses.definition_en: The foundational principle of treating others with the same care, respect, and protection one desires for oneself.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u se ke ua jara bara ba batho ba heno ka pelo; ’me u rate oa heno joalokaha u ithata.
usage_example.english: ...nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself.

senses.definition_en: Instruments of measurement that are accurate and not tampered with, representing integrity in trade.

usage_example.sesotho: Le lokela ho ba le sekala se nepahetseng, boima bo nepahetseng...
usage_example.english: You shall have honest scales, honest weights...

headword_sesotho.orthographic: mali a bona a holim ’a bona
headword_sesotho.tone_marked: mālī ā bōnā ā hōlīm ’ā bōnā

syllables.orthographic: ma-li a bo-na a ho-lim 'a bo-na

senses.definition_en: A legal formula indicating that the person executed is solely responsible for their own death due to their crimes; no bloodguilt is on the executioner.

usage_example.sesotho: Ruri ba lokela ho bolaoa. Mali a bona a holim ’a bona.
usage_example.english: They shall surely be put to death. Their blood shall be upon them.

morphology.derivation: To gain wealth or to come into possession of land.

senses.definition_en: To take ownership of the land promised by God as a permanent heritage.

usage_example.sesotho: Le tla rua naha ea tsona, ’me ke tla le fa eona hore le e rue.
usage_example.english: You shall inherit their land, and I will give it to you to possess.

senses.definition_en: The supreme religious leader in Israel, uniquely anointed to enter the Most Holy Place.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha e le moprista ea phahameng... ha aa lokela ho lumella hore hlooho ea hae e be mahlantholla.
usage_example.english: He who is the high priest... shall not uncover his head.

morphology.derivation: Refers to a spot, mark, or physical flaw.

senses.definition_en: A physical deformity or imperfection that disqualified a priest from serving at the altar.

usage_example.sesotho: Ha ho monna... ea nang le sekoli ea tla atamela ho hlahisa bohobe ba Molimo oa hae.
usage_example.english: No man... who has any defect, may approach to offer the bread of his God.

senses.definition_en: To treat something sacred with a lack of reverence or to make it common/unclean.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba se ke ba hlompholla lebitso la ka le halalelang.
usage_example.english: ...that they do not profane My holy name.

senses.definition_en: A sacrifice brought spontaneously as an expression of devotion or gratitude rather than as a requirement of law.

usage_example.sesotho: ...kapa bakeng sa linyehelo leha e le life tsa bona tsa boithatelo...
usage_example.english: ...or for any of his freewill offerings.

senses.definition_en: A sacred assembly of people called together for worship and to abstain from ordinary work.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le lokela ho ba le phomolo e feletseng, sehopotso se etsoang ka molumo oa terompeta, kopano e halalelang.
usage_example.english: ...you shall have a sabbath-rest, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.

morphology.derivation: Plural of 'phephe' (a temporary shelter or hut).

senses.definition_en: Temporary shelters made of branches used during the Feast of Tabernacles to commemorate the wilderness wandering.

usage_example.sesotho: Le lokela ho lula maphepheng ka matsatsi a supileng.
usage_example.english: You shall dwell in booths for seven days.

morphology.derivation: To insult or treat with contempt, specifically regarding the Divine.

senses.definition_en: The act of speaking sacrilegiously about God or sacred things; a capital offense in ancient Israel.

usage_example.sesotho: Mora oa mosali oa Moiseraele a qala ho nyefola Lebitso le ho le rohaka.
usage_example.english: And the Israelite woman's son blasphemed the name [of the Lord] and cursed.

senses.definition_en: The principle that a person who has injured another person is to be penalized to a similar degree.

usage_example.sesotho: leihlo bakeng sa leihlo, leino bakeng sa leino; sekoli sa mofuta o tšoanang... ke sona se lokelang ho etsoa ho eena.
usage_example.english: eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused disfigurement... so shall it be done to him.

morphology.derivation: Derived from the word for a ram's horn.

senses.definition_en: The fiftieth year occurring after seven weeks of years, characterized by the return of property and the manumission of slaves.

usage_example.sesotho: Selemo sa mashome a mahlano e tla ba Jubile bakeng sa lōna.
usage_example.english: That fiftieth year shall be a Jubilee to you.

morphology.derivation: Reversal of 'reka' (to buy); to undo a sale.

senses.definition_en: To recover ownership of property or a person by paying a specific price.

usage_example.sesotho: ...morekolli ea amanang haufi-ufi le eena a tle ’me a rekolle seo mor’abo a se rekisitseng.
usage_example.english: ...and if his redeeming relative comes to redeem it, then he may redeem what his brother sold.

senses.definition_en: A solemn utterance intended to invoke a supernatural power to inflict harm or punishment on someone.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke tla lokela ho le shapa ka makhetlo a supileng bakeng sa libe tsa lōna.
usage_example.english: I will punish you seven times more for your sins.

morphology.derivation: Refers to a place that is ruined, abandoned, or empty.

senses.definition_en: A state of complete emptiness or destruction, specifically referring to the land during exile.

usage_example.sesotho: ...naha ea lōna e tla ba lesupi, ’me metse ea lōna e tla ba lesupi.
usage_example.english: ...your land shall be desolate and your cities waste.

senses.definition_en: A voluntary promise made to God to perform some act or make some offering.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba motho a etsa boitlamo bo khethehileng ha a nehelana ka meea ho Jehova...
usage_example.english: When a man consecrates by a vow certain persons to the LORD...

senses.definition_en: An official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

usage_example.sesotho: Balang phutheho eohle ea bara ba Iseraele ho ea ka malapa a bona.
usage_example.english: Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel by their families.

morphology.derivation: A physical marker or sign used to identify a tribal group.

senses.definition_en: A flag or banner used by a military unit or a tribe to identify their location in the camp.

usage_example.sesotho: ...motho e mong le e mong a be sehlopheng sa habo.
usage_example.english: ...everyone by his own standard.

senses.definition_en: The direction toward the point of the horizon where the sun rises at the equinoxes.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba hlomang liahelo ka nģ’a bochabela... e tla ba sehlopha sa Juda.
usage_example.english: On the east side, toward the rising of the sun, those of the standard of Judah shall camp.

senses.definition_en: The action of regaining or gaining possession of something in exchange for payment.

usage_example.sesotho: E le tefo ea thekollo ea ba... fetang palo ea Balevi.
usage_example.english: And for the redemption of those... who are more than the number of the Levites.

morphology.derivation: Tools or instruments used for work.

senses.definition_en: The sacred furniture and tools used within the Tabernacle for worship and sacrifice.

usage_example.sesotho: Mosebetsi oa bona e ne e le Areka le tafole le seluloana sa lebone...
usage_example.english: Their duty included the ark, the table, the lampstand...

senses.definition_en: A piece of fabric used to conceal or protect a sacred object from view.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba theole lesira le sireletsang ba koahele areka ea bopaki ka lona.
usage_example.english: ...they shall take down the covering veil and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.

morphology.derivation: Long wooden rods used for transport.

senses.definition_en: Wooden beams inserted into rings on the sides of sacred furniture to allow them to be carried without being touched.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ba se behe holim ’a palo.
usage_example.english: ...and put it on a carrying beam.

morphology.derivation: From 'lefa' (to pay) or 'teletso' (act of paying back).

senses.definition_en: The restoration of something lost or stolen to its proper owner, or a penalty paid for a wrong.

usage_example.sesotho: ...a khutlise se lekanang le molato oa hae se feletse, hape a se eketse ka karolo ea bohlano.
usage_example.english: ...he shall make restitution for his trespass in full, plus one-fifth of it.

senses.definition_en: Breaking a promise or a covenant; acting against the trust of a partner or God.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba mosali oa monna leha e le ofe a kheloha ka hore a etse ketso ea ho se tšepahale ho eena...
usage_example.english: If any man's wife goes astray and behaves unfaithfully toward him...

senses.definition_en: A person who voluntarily took a vow of separation and service to God, marked by specific abstentions.

usage_example.sesotho: ...haeba monna kapa mosali a etsa boitlamo bo khethehileng ba ho phela joaloka Monazari oa Jehova...
usage_example.english: ...when either a man or woman takes the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD...

morphology.derivation: State of being at peace or satisfied.

senses.definition_en: A state of harmony, safety, and prosperity; the complete well-being granted by God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...’me a le abele khotso.
usage_example.english: ...and give you peace.

morphology.derivation: From 'hakola' (to perform a ceremony for the first time).

senses.definition_en: The formal act of setting aside or consecrating a building or altar for divine service.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale marenana a etsa nyehelo ha ho khakoloa aletare...
usage_example.english: Now the leaders offered the dedication offering for the altar...

senses.definition_en: The part of the body where the arm attaches; used here as the method for carrying the holiest objects.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba ne ba jara ka mahetla.
usage_example.english: They carried [them] on [their] shoulders.

senses.definition_en: Metalwork created by beating a single piece of gold into shape rather than joining separate parts.

usage_example.sesotho: Se ne se entsoe ka thepa e teiloeng ka hamore.
usage_example.english: It was made of hammered work.

senses.definition_en: The time of day immediately following sunset; specifically the window for the Passover sacrifice.

usage_example.sesotho: ...letsatsing la leshome le metso e mene la khoeli ena pakeng tsa lishoalane tse peli.
usage_example.english: ...on the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight.

senses.definition_en: An authoritative instruction or direction that must be followed.

usage_example.sesotho: Bara ba Iseraele ba ne ba tsamaea ka taelo ea Jehova.
usage_example.english: At the command of the LORD the children of Israel would journey.

senses.definition_en: Metal that has been shaped by repeated blows from a hammer, indicating craftsmanship and strength.

usage_example.sesotho: U li etse ka thepa e teiloeng ka hamore...
usage_example.english: You shall make them of hammered work...

senses.definition_en: The military formation at the back of a column that protects the group from attacks from behind.

usage_example.sesotho: ...joalokaha se ne se e-na le balebeli ba ka morao bakeng sa batho bohle.
usage_example.english: ...as the rear guard of all the camps.

senses.definition_en: An intense, often selfish or irrational desire for something one does not have.

usage_example.sesotho: ...moo ba ile ba pata sechaba se ileng sa bontša takatso e feteletseng.
usage_example.english: ...there they buried the people who had yielded to craving.

senses.definition_en: The divine influence or power of God bestowed upon individuals for leadership or prophecy.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke tla nka o mong oa moea oa ka o ho uena ke o behe ho bona.
usage_example.english: I will take of the Spirit that is upon you and will put it upon them.

senses.definition_en: The quality of being patient, long-suffering, and submissive to divine will without pride.

usage_example.sesotho: Monna enoa Moshe o ne a le bonolo haholo.
usage_example.english: Now the man Moses was very humble.

senses.definition_en: Cities protected by high walls and defensive structures to prevent invasion.

usage_example.sesotho: ...le metse eo ea liqhobosheane e meholo haholo.
usage_example.english: ...and the cities are fortified and very large.

senses.definition_en: A small insect; used here as a metaphor for insignificance and vulnerability in the face of giants.

usage_example.sesotho: ...re ileng ra tšoana le marutle.
usage_example.english: ...we were like grasshoppers.

senses.definition_en: The dead body of a human or animal, often used here to describe the tragic end of the rebellious generation.

usage_example.sesotho: Litopo tsa lōna li tla oa lefeelleng lena.
usage_example.english: Your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness.

senses.definition_en: The act of granting forgiveness or cancelling a debt/sin based on a plea.

usage_example.sesotho: Kea tšoarela ho ea ka lentsoe la hao.
usage_example.english: I have pardoned according to your word.

senses.definition_en: A libation of wine poured out as an accompaniment to an animal sacrifice.

usage_example.sesotho: Le lokela ho fana ka veine e le nyehelo ea seno...
usage_example.english: You shall prepare wine as a drink offering...

morphology.idiomatic: Acting with full knowledge and intent to disobey.

senses.definition_en: Acting with pride and intentional defiance against a known law or authority.

usage_example.sesotho: Empa moea o etsang ntho ka boomo... o nyefola Jehova.
usage_example.english: But the person who does anything presumptuously... brings reproach on the LORD.

senses.definition_en: The right to lead or command, which Kora and his followers challenged.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke hobane’ng ha le iphahamisetsa phutheho ea Jehova?
usage_example.english: Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?

senses.definition_en: An act performed to appease divine wrath and reconcile the people to God.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u ee ho phutheho ka potlako ’me u koahele libe tsa eona.
usage_example.english: ...go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them.

morphology.derivation: A piece of wood used for walking or as a symbol of tribal rule.

senses.definition_en: An object representing the authority of a tribal leader or 'morenana'.

usage_example.sesotho: ...u nke molamu o le mong ho bona bakeng sa lelapa ka leng.
usage_example.english: ...get from them a rod from each father's house.

morphology.meaning: To go out or disappear completely.

senses.definition_en: To die or be completely wiped out, often in a context of judgment.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale re tla shoa, re tla timela.
usage_example.english: Surely we die, we perish.

senses.definition_en: An everlasting, unbreakable agreement that does not decay.

usage_example.sesotho: Ke selekane sa letsoai ho isa nakong e sa lekanyetsoang.
usage_example.english: It is a covenant of salt forever.

morphology.meaning: To cause oneself to be clean.

senses.definition_en: To undergo a ritual process to remove spiritual or ceremonial defilement.

usage_example.sesotho: Ea joalo o lokela ho itlhoekisa ka ’ona ka letsatsi la boraro.
usage_example.english: He shall purify himself with it on the third day.

morphology.meaning: To cause something to be regarded as holy.

senses.definition_en: To show God's holiness through obedience and honor, which Moses failed to do at the rock.

usage_example.sesotho: Kahobane ha lea ka la... nkhalaletse ka pel’a mahlo a bara ba Iseraele.
usage_example.english: Because you did not... hallow Me in the eyes of the children of Israel.

senses.definition_en: An established trade route used by travelers and armies in ancient Transjordan.

usage_example.sesotho: Re tla tsamaea tseleng ea morena.
usage_example.english: We will go along the King’s Highway.

senses.definition_en: Describing the serpents whose bites were deadly and caused burning pain.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a romela linoha tse chefo har’a sechaba.
usage_example.english: Jehovah sent fiery serpents among the people.

senses.definition_en: Someone who remains alive after a battle or disaster.

usage_example.sesotho: ...ho fihlela ho se mophonyohi ea setseng ho eena.
usage_example.english: ...until there was no survivor left him.

senses.definition_en: A celestial being sent by God to deliver a message or execute judgment.

usage_example.sesotho: ...lengeloi la Jehova la ema tseleng ho mo hanyetsa.
usage_example.english: ...the angel of the LORD stood in the way to oppose him.

morphology.meaning: To undo what has been done.

senses.definition_en: To cancel or overturn a decree or blessing, which Balaam claims is impossible regarding God's word.

usage_example.sesotho: ...O hlohonolofatse, ’me nke ke ka ho etsolla.
usage_example.english: ...He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it.

morphology.derivation: The practice of using supernatural power for harm.

senses.definition_en: Occult practices or spells intended to cause misfortune.

usage_example.sesotho: Etsoe ha ho mantsoe a boloi a bakelang Jakobo bomalimabe.
usage_example.english: For there is no sorcery against Jacob.

morphology.note: Literally 'sons', but used for children of a nation.

senses.definition_en: The offspring of a specific ancestor; members of a tribe.

usage_example.sesotho: Bara ba Iseraele ba tloha Kadeshe.
usage_example.english: The children of Israel departed from Kadesh.

morphology.meaning: To send to or for someone.

senses.definition_en: To cause a person or message to go to a destination.

usage_example.sesotho: Balake a romela manģosa ho Balame.
usage_example.english: Balak sent messengers to Balaam.

senses.definition_en: The whole body of the people of Israel as a community.

usage_example.sesotho: Joale ho ne ho se na metsi bakeng sa phutheho.
usage_example.english: Now there was no water for the congregation.

morphology.note: Can mean to sit, to stay, or to live/dwell.

senses.definition_en: To reside in a place for a period of time.

usage_example.sesotho: ...’me sechaba sa lula Kadeshe.
usage_example.english: ...and the people dwelt in Kadesh.

senses.definition_en: To utterly defeat or destroy the power of an enemy.

usage_example.sesotho: O tla thumanya mahlakore a phatla ea Moabe.
usage_example.english: He shall crush the forehead of Moab.

morphology.note: Used here for divine jealousy—protecting a sacred bond.

senses.definition_en: A fierce protectiveness of God's exclusive worship.

usage_example.sesotho: ...kahobane o ne a e-na le poulo bakeng sa Molimo oa hae.
usage_example.english: ...because he was zealous for his God.

morphology.meaning: That which falls upon the people.

senses.definition_en: A widespread disease or calamity sent as a judgment.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba seoa se ea emisa har’a bara ba Iseraele.
usage_example.english: So the plague was stayed among the children of Israel.

morphology.note: Used for both male and female parents in biblical context.

senses.definition_en: To procreate; to be the biological parent of.

usage_example.sesotho: Adama a tsoala sethole.
usage_example.english: Adam begot a son.

senses.definition_en: A male offspring; often used to denote a member of a tribe or nation.

usage_example.sesotho: Bara ba Iseraele ba tloha Egepeta.
usage_example.english: The sons of Israel departed Egypt.

morphology.meaning: Men of great age or status.

senses.definition_en: Traditional leaders of a tribe or community charged with governance.

usage_example.sesotho: Moshe a bitsa banna ba baholo ba Iseraele.
usage_example.english: Moses called the elders of Israel.

senses.definition_en: To place something over an object; to hide or protect.

usage_example.sesotho: Bona! Sechaba se koahetse lefatše.
usage_example.english: Look! The people have covered the earth.

senses.definition_en: To respond to a question, statement, or prayer.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Balame oa araba o re ho Balake...
usage_example.english: Then Balaam answered and said to Balak...

morphology.note: Always used in the plural class (Ma-).

senses.definition_en: The liquid that descends from the clouds as rain; found in rivers and springs.

usage_example.sesotho: O ba tlisitse metsi lefikeng.
usage_example.english: He brought them waters out of the rock.

senses.definition_en: A large group of domestic animals, especially sheep or goats.

usage_example.sesotho: Mehlape ea rōna e ke ke ea fula masimong a lōna.
usage_example.english: Our flocks shall not graze in your fields.

senses.definition_en: A social division in a traditional society consisting of families linked by social, economic, or blood ties.

usage_example.sesotho: Leloko la Juda le ne le le leholo.
usage_example.english: The tribe of Judah was large.

senses.definition_en: Property, land, or rank which is passed down from an ancestor.

usage_example.sesotho: Naha e tla aroleloa e le lefa la bona.
usage_example.english: The land shall be divided as their inheritance.

senses.definition_en: To get up from sleep or a sitting position; to begin an action.

usage_example.sesotho: Eaba Moshe oa tsoha, o ea tenteng.
usage_example.english: Then Moses arose and went to the tent.

senses.definition_en: A nomadic tribe known for attacking the Israelites; symbolic of perpetual enmity.

usage_example.sesotho: Amaleke ke oa pele har'a lichaba.
usage_example.english: Amalek was first among the nations.

senses.definition_en: Male siblings; also used for kinsmen or fellow tribesmen.

usage_example.sesotho: Josefa a re ho banab'abo...
usage_example.english: Joseph said to his brothers...

senses.definition_en: To carry or conduct someone or something to a place.

usage_example.sesotho: O re tlisitse naheng ena.
usage_example.english: He brought us into this land.

senses.definition_en: The land between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea; the Promised Land.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a ba tšepisa naha ea Kanana.
usage_example.english: Jehovah promised them the land of Canaan.

senses.definition_en: To give an authoritative order or requirement.

usage_example.sesotho: Feela joalo ka ha Jehova a laetse Moshe.
usage_example.english: Just as Jehovah commanded Moses.

senses.definition_en: Two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicles used in ancient warfare.

usage_example.sesotho: Faro a lelekisa Iseraele ka likoloi tsa hae.
usage_example.english: Pharaoh pursued Israel with his chariots.

senses.definition_en: Female offspring; women of a particular family or nation.

usage_example.sesotho: Barali ba Selofehade ba tla ho Moshe.
usage_example.english: The daughters of Zelophehad came to Moses.

senses.definition_en: To leave a place; to begin a journey.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba tloha thabeng ea Sinai.
usage_example.english: They departed from Mount Sinai.

senses.definition_en: The land in northeast Africa where Israel was enslaved and from which they were delivered.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a ntša Iseraele naheng ea Egepeta.
usage_example.english: Jehovah brought Israel out of the land of Egypt.

senses.definition_en: The twin brother of Jacob and the ancestor of the Edomites.

usage_example.sesotho: Esau a rekisa tolohelo ea hae.
usage_example.english: Esau sold his birthright.

senses.definition_en: To consume food; often used in the context of sacrificial meals or manna.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba ja manna lilemo tse mashome a mane.
usage_example.english: They ate manna for forty years.

senses.definition_en: Groups of people related by blood; clans within a tribe.

usage_example.sesotho: Bana ke maloko a lapa la Rubene.
usage_example.english: These are the families of the house of Reuben.

senses.definition_en: To discover or come upon something; to obtain favor.

usage_example.sesotho: Haeba ke fumane mohau mahlong a hao...
usage_example.english: If I have found favor in your eyes...

senses.definition_en: An amphibious animal; used as a plague in Egypt.

usage_example.sesotho: Naha ea tlala linqanqane.
usage_example.english: The land was filled with frogs.

senses.definition_en: To provide or present something to another; to grant a land or law.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a ba fa naha eo a e tšepisitseng.
usage_example.english: Jehovah gave them the land he had promised.

senses.definition_en: Items of clothing; often refers to the sacred vestments of the priesthood.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba hlatsoa liaparo tsa bona.
usage_example.english: They washed their garments.

senses.definition_en: The fruit of the vine; used as a sign of the land's fertility.

usage_example.sesotho: Ba kha sehlopha sa morara Eshekole.
usage_example.english: They cut a cluster of grapes at Eshcol.

senses.definition_en: To perceive sound; to obey or pay attention to a command.

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova a utloa sello sa bona.
usage_example.english: Jehovah heard their cry.

senses.definition_en: The upper part of the body; also used to denote leaders or chiefs.

usage_example.sesotho: Lihlooho tsa malapa a Iseraele.
usage_example.english: The heads of the households of Israel.
